title: Sustained-burst smoothing and inter-zone epoch harmonization for reserved tenants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Reserved tenants frequently run into billing and availability skew when their usage straddles daily or monthly reset boundaries across regions. Small clock drift, cross-zone DAG delays, and transient master failovers cause disputed token accounting and surprising throttles during sustained bursts. Existing rolling-window logic applies hard resets at zone-local epoch boundaries which can lead to double-counting or missed top-ups during cross-region handoffs.

Goal: Implement a smoothing layer and cross-zone epoch harmonization to ensure reserved capacity tenants see deterministic, fair, and auditable quota behavior during sustained bursts and when requests cross region/zone boundaries. The solution should reduce disputed invoices, avoid transient throttles caused by boundary jitter, and remain cost-predictable for customers and billing.

High-level approach:
1) Per-tenant rolling-credit-smoothing: Maintain a small exponential moving average (EMA) of consumed tokens and effective burst headroom for each tenant. The EMA will be used as a tie-breaker when usage samples are ambiguous during epoch transitions.
2) Inter-zone epoch harmonization: Introduce a short-lived overlap window (configurable, default 2s) around reset boundaries where zone-local reset actions are deferred and reconciled using a single authoritative ledger update propagated via the quota coordination service.
3) Drift attestation: When a zone boundary transition occurs, record clock attestation metadata (source NTP offset, leader election version, last sync id) on the ledger entry to make audit and chargebacks deterministic.
4) Safe rollback and observability: All reconciliations are append-only with a rollback tombstone entry to support safe replay and automatic reconciliation in case of partial commits. Add new telemetry and alerts to detect reconciliation rate and outstanding tombstones.

Design trade-offs:
- Positive: Avoids customer-visible throttles due to transient clock skew; reduces disputed billing; preserves strong audit trail.
- Negative: Adds a small amount of coordination traffic and slightly increased write amplification on the quota ledger during boundary windows. May add ~0.5-1% token accounting latency for the boundary window.

Implementation plan:
Phase 1 (experiment):
- Implement EMA smoothing in quota-service read path as opt-in flag for a small pilot group.
- Add overlap window gating in each zone; for now, only on reserved-capacity clusters.
- Emit new metrics: quota.reconcile.attempts, quota.reconcile.latency, quota.tombstones.pending, quota.ema.offset.

Phase 2 (wider roll):
- Wire the authoritative ledger reconciler that coordinates the overlap window commit across zones.
- Persist drift attestation metadata on commits and expose via audit logs.
- Implement graceful fallback: If reconciliation fails, fallback to deterministic conservative settle (deduct smaller of two counts) and create dispute ticket automatically.

Phase 3 (hardening):
- Automate periodic tombstone pruning and add backfill job for zones with missed updates.
- Run full regression against billing ETL to verify no revenue leakage.
- Update docs and support playbooks.

Data migration / compatibility: The EMA state is lightweight and can be backfilled from recent token usage windows (last 1-2 hours). The ledger schema requires adding two fields (drift_attestation, tombstone_id) which are backwards compatible because older reconciler will ignore unknown fields.

Success metrics:
- < 0.1% disputed invoices attributable to epoch transition in pilot tenants within 30 days.
- Reduced transient throttle events near boundary windows by >= 80% in pilot clusters.
- Latency impact of boundary operations < 1s p95 additional latency.

Acceptance criteria:
acceptance_criteria: Pilot enables smoothing for at least 10 reserved tenants without billing disputes for 30 days
Reconciliation overlap window prevents double-charges in cross-zone handoffs during synthetic fault injection tests
New telemetry surfaces tombstones and reconciliation failures and alerting is in place
Automated rollback path triggers and recovers without human intervention in injected failure tests
